item.title: LinkedIn buys Pulse
item.description:
The largest professional networking site is broadening its horizons, on the 18th LinkedIn announced the purchase of the mobile application Pulse, which works as an aggregator of internet content, such as news and blogs.

LinkedIn paid 90 million dollars for the application that emerged from an academic project by Ankit and Akshay in 2010 at Stanford University and was currently held by the California company Alphonso Labs.

The amount will be paid 90% in shares and 10% in cash, the social network said, according to it, Pulse has more than 30 million users from around 190 countries and distributes content from more than 750 publishers.

item.title: Startups in Brazil
item.description:
The dream of Brazil’s IT visionaries is closer to becoming reality, on April 15 a StartUp program created by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI) was launched by the government, the call for applications from interested startups is on the Start-Up Brasil program’s website (2013 call for applications, now offline).

Around 30% of the competing startups will be international, applications open on April 25 and close on May 31, the results of this first stage will be released from June 25 on the CNPq website and in the Official Gazette of the Union.

item.title: Android was software for cameras
item.description:
That’s right, Android began with a focus on cameras, according to Andy Rubin, creator of the original system, the initial intention of his invention was to reach the photography market.

However, Google acquired Android Inc in 2005 and the plans gradually changed and became more ambitious, making the platform the success it is today.

Recently Android reached 1.5 million activations per day, to think that the story could have been different, Android an operating system for digital cameras.

item.title: Smartphone prices will drop in Brazil
item.description:
With the aim of making smartphones (which have internet connectivity among their functions) more accessible to lower-income groups, the Government approved a decree today that reduces the PIS and COFINS rates on these devices to zero. This measure will bring consumers a price reduction of up to 30% compared with imported devices, and only devices costing less than R$ 1,500.00 and manufactured in Brazil will qualify for the measure.

The price drop is expected next week, since an ordinance with the specifications of the mobile devices that will qualify for this measure still needs to be published.

item.title: Get to know Facebook Home
item.description:
On April 04 (last week), the launch event took place for Facebook’s new functionality called “Home”. This new feature was presented by Mark Zunckerberg himself, the functionality is available for smartphones running the Android operating system.

With the aim of turning any phone into a personalized device on the social network, Home will use the phone’s home screen as the Facebook homepage, overlaying the other applications on your device, so when you turn on your device you’ll be connected to Facebook.

item.title: The viral Harlem Shake
item.description:
The viral hit of the moment has already reached 1 billion views in 40 days, the number of views wasn’t achieved with just one posted video, but through scenes from other videos, according to the company Visible Measures, just the ten most popular versions of “Harlem Shake” account for a total of 336 million views.

However, this viral hit ended up causing some trouble, for example, at a mining company in Australia 15 miners were fired after posting a video of the dance during working hours and at their workplace. Here in Brazil, in Goiânia, a school suspended students who made the Harlem Shake video in the bathroom. However, some companies joined the trend and got everyone dancing, among them NASA and Facebook.

item.title: Do you know what Coworking is?
item.description: Coworking means sharing workspace with other professionals. This movement emerged in 2005 with a software engineer, Brad Neuberg, he was tired of working from home and got together with some friends from different fields, and this way they set up an independent office where everyone shares the expenses, but without mixing their businesses. After this, many other coworking spaces started appearing, today there are around 600 different types of coworking.

item.title: The Pirate Bay leads its segment
item.description:
In 2011 the Torret Freak website conducted a survey of file-sharing sites that showed the cyberlocker model dominating the ‘market’. 4shared was the leader, while The Pirate Bay occupied only sixth place.

Today the story is different, Pirate Bay has taken first place, according to Torrent Freak’s analysis, the title was acquired through the declining popularity of hosting sites such as 4Shared and Megaupload, after Megaupload’s closure and anti-piracy measures these sites saw a drop in usage. Making Pirate Bay the world’s most famous and most used site for downloading files.

item.title: Shortage of IT professionals in Brazil
item.description: Today IT professionals in Brazil face a broad job market with few qualified competitors. However, the areas with the fewest qualified professionals are network management, IP telephony and online security. This information comes from consultancy IDC, which expects a shortage of these professionals in Brazil’s job market. This year there is a shortage of around 40 thousand technology professionals, and for 2015 an increase to 117 thousand open positions is predicted.

item.title: Tablets as Tools in the Corporate Environment
item.description: According to a survey by consultancy IDC, in 2012 tablet use grew by 159% in the home and 303% in the Corporate environment compared with 2011, this growth was generated by the range of functionality mobile devices have. Today we can manage our bank accounts, make payments without moving, using only an internet connection and an application provided by the bank, eliminating the possibility of losing our lunch break in a queue.

item.title: Apple Macbook Pro 15" with Retina Display
item.description:
Every day new products are created, some stand out, others not so much. Recently I bought the revolutionary 15-inch MacBook Pro with Retina display.

Apple’s product line is very well respected in the market, the product quality is excellent, and I mean that starting with its box.

The new MacBook Pro is quite a light laptop, measuring 1.8 centimeters thick and weighing just 2 kilos, the same as the 13-inch model.

item.title: Git Hub reaches 3 million users
item.description:
The web hosting service GitHub announced that it passed the three-million-user mark.

This site has social network features such as feeds, followers, wiki and a graph showing how developers work with versions of their repositories. It also has a service called Gist, where developers can distribute source code, similar to Paste Bin.

In 2008 – when the service was founded – it reached one million users, and in fewer than twelve months reached two million registered users. Now the service has reached three million users in fewer than six months. These events represent the service’s importance and popularity within the developer community.

item.title: Internet Explorer has less than 50% of the market
item.description:
Microsoft’s Internet Explorer browser had less than 50% market share in September, recording the biggest decline in its history. According to market analysis company StatCounter, global browser usage was 49.87%, a much lower figure compared with when the program won the battle against Netscape in the 90s, capturing most of the market.

StatCounter also says that Mozilla’s Firefox, in second place, has 31.5% of the browser market, while Google’s Chrome is third, with 11.54%. However, the program has tripled its usage since the same period last year. According to a report from the Softpedia website, Chrome is the fastest-growing browser. The rest of the market is divided among browsers with smaller shares, such as Opera and Apple’s Safari.
